fullAnalysis: Puzzle #679 gives you five clues — Toad, Piranha Plant, Bowser, Luigi, and Princess Peach — that land on a clean franchise category: Characters in Super Mario. The board mixes a friendly mushroom-person, a dangerous plant species, the main villain, a hero brother, and a royal princess, which makes the surface read feel jumbled until you recognise the shared universe.

The broader rule is that franchise puzzles never require every clue to play the same role. Heroes, villains, allies, and generic enemies can all belong to the same answer as long as they inhabit the same fictional world. Resist the urge to narrow the category to 'Mario heroes' or 'Mario villains' — the correct answer is always the most inclusive shared rule that fits all five clues.
solutionNarrative: I spotted Bowser and Luigi immediately and the franchise was obvious within seconds. Mario was the clear hypothesis, so I tested the remaining three against it: Toad, Princess Peach, Piranha Plant. Toad and Peach confirmed cleanly without any hesitation.

Piranha Plant gave me a brief pause — it is a species, not a named individual, and its presence alongside personality-driven characters felt inconsistent. Then I reminded myself that Pinpoint regularly includes enemy types as representatives of a fictional world. Piranha Plant appears throughout the Mario series, which is all that matters. Five for five, answer locked.

wordHints.Toad: Toad is a core Mario character and one of the clearest franchise anchors in the set.

wordHints.Bowser: Bowser is Mario's most recognizable villain and typically the fastest clue for identifying the franchise.
wordHints.Luigi: Luigi is Mario's brother and co-star, making the Mario connection unmistakable alongside Bowser.
wordHints.Princess Peach: Princess Peach is a central Mario character who closes the set with a final, unambiguous franchise confirmation.

lessons.title: Franchise boards mix heroes and villains on purpose
lessons.body: Toad and Princess Peach are heroes; Bowser and Piranha Plant are antagonists. Designers blend character types to disguise the shared universe, so always check whether a fictional world — not a character role — is what connects the clues.

lessons.title: Lock the franchise with your two strongest clues first
lessons.body: Bowser and Luigi together are an almost unbeatable anchor pair for Mario. When two clues point unmistakably to one franchise, apply that franchise to the other three before exploring any other hypothesis.

lessons.title: Species and enemy types count as characters
lessons.body: Piranha Plant is a species, not a named individual, yet it qualifies as a Mario character. Pinpoint regularly uses generic enemy types and creature families as representatives of a franchise, so do not disqualify a clue just because it lacks a personal name.

faqs.question: What is the LinkedIn Pinpoint answer for Puzzle #679?
faqs.answer: The answer for Puzzle #679 is Characters in Super Mario.

faqs.question: Why does Piranha Plant fit this board?
faqs.answer: Piranha Plant is a well-known recurring enemy in the Mario series, so it belongs in the same character family as Bowser, Luigi, and Princess Peach.

faqs.question: What clue makes the answer easiest to spot?
faqs.answer: Bowser and Luigi together are the strongest anchor pair — both are central Mario characters, and the franchise is immediately obvious once you see them side by side.
